title: LCATS: LLM-Guided Constraint-Aware Tabular Data Synthesis

problem.claim: Tabular data synthesis must preserve both global statistical fidelity and local domain-specific logical constraints.

gap.claim: Diffusion-based methods may violate hard logical constraints, while LLM-based methods may suffer distributional drift that reduces global fidelity.

contributions.claim: LCATS is an end-to-end framework that decouples global distribution modeling from local constraint enforcement.

The framework uses an LLM to discover and validate executable constraint checks, a diffusion model for synthesis, and constrained weighted optimization with iterative feedback for repairing violations while limiting distributional distortion.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on seven benchmark datasets reportedly show strong overall performance against diffusion-based, LLM-based, and hybrid baselines on the stated precision, recall, and downstream predictive-performance measures.
The authors report zero constraint violations.
The code is reported to be available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: The task is framed as jointly preserving global statistical characteristics and local logical constraints in synthetic tabular records.
Existing diffusion-based and LLM-based approaches are described as exhibiting complementary weaknesses in constraint adherence and global fidelity.
LCATS is introduced as a framework that separates global distribution modeling from local constraint enforcement.
Its modules discover and validate constraints, generate data with diffusion, repair violating records through constrained optimization, and use iterative feedback to reduce distortion.
The authors report benchmark comparisons, zero constraint violations, and code availability.

source_observation.claim: Separating global distribution modeling from local constraint enforcement is the central design choice in LCATS.

interpretation.claim: A modular pipeline may address competing synthesis objectives by assigning statistical fidelity and logical validity to different mechanisms.

application.claim: For constrained tabular synthesis, consider generating records with a distribution-focused model and applying validated, optimization-based repairs afterward.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition is preferable for datasets whose constraints are poorly specified, non-executable, or highly coupled with the data distribution.

unknowns: The precision and recall metric names are unavailable in the supplied abstract units.
The abstract does not identify the seven benchmark datasets or quantify comparative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, ablation results, or independent verification of the reported performance and zero-violation outcome.
